english: May I use the bathroom?
tip: The '-abilir' slice adds can or may: 'kullanabilir' = can use, from 'kullan' plus 'abilir'.

english: Is this place empty?
tip: To turn an adjective into a yes/no question, add 'mu' after it: 'boş mu' = is it empty.

english: They will go to the hospital soon.
tip: The '-e' ending marks a destination: 'hastaneye' = to the hospital, from 'hastane' plus 'ye'.

english: She just finished cooking dinner.
tip: To finish doing something, the action takes '-meyi' before 'bitirdi': 'pişirmeyi bitirdi' = finished cooking.

english: They started in the kitchen last week.
tip: The '-tan' ending means from: 'mutfaktan' = from the kitchen, from 'mutfak' plus 'tan'.

english: There are twelve eggs in the box.
tip: 'var' means there is and sits at the end, with the place in the '-da' form: 'kutuda ... var' = there is in the box.

english: The butterfly flew from flower to flower.
tip: The from and to pair uses '-ten' then '-e': 'çiçekten çiçeğe' = from flower to flower.

english: The tourists ate the baklava at the restaurant.
tip: The '-yı' ending marks a specific, definite object: 'baklavayı' = the baklava, a known particular one.

english: How many fossils are displayed in the paleontology museum?
tip: After 'kaç' meaning how many, the noun stays singular: 'kaç fosil', never 'kaç fosiller'.

english: When I was little I used to love riding a bicycle.
tip: The '-ken' ending means when or while: 'küçükken' = when I was little.

target: Arkadaşım Beyoğlu'nda yeni bir restoran açtı.
english: My friend opened a new restaurant in Beyoğlu.
tip: A proper name takes an apostrophe before any suffix: 'Beyoğlu'nda' = in Beyoğlu.

target: Bu kışın en soğuk günü bugünmüş.
english: Apparently today is the coldest day of this winter.
tip: The '-müş' ending marks hearsay or a fresh realization: 'bugünmüş' = apparently it is today.

target: Otobüse geç kaldığım için koşarak çıktım.
english: I ran out because I was late for the bus.
tip: The '-arak' ending turns a verb into by doing it: 'koşarak çıktım' = I went out running.

target: Park ile okul arasında bir fırın var.
english: There is a bakery between the park and the school.
tip: Between X and Y is X 'ile' Y 'arasında', with 'arasında' last: 'park ile okul arasında' = between the park and the school.

target: Bu eski bina yıkılacak ve yerine yenisi yapılacak.
english: This old building will be demolished and a new one built in its place.
tip: The '-il' slice makes a verb passive: 'yıkılacak' = will be demolished, with no doer named.

target: Öğrenciler hafta içi plaja gitmek için izin aldı.
english: The students got permission to go to the beach during the week.
tip: After a base verb, 'için' means in order to: 'gitmek için' = in order to go.

english: Can I try this on?
tip: Ability comes from '-ebilir': 'dene' (try) plus '-ebilir' gives 'deneyebilir', and a 'y' slips in between the two vowels.

english: Which languages can you speak?
tip: A specific object takes '-i': 'dilleri' means those particular languages, not 'diller' for languages in general.

english: The ticket costs forty-five lira.
tip: No word for costs or is: 'bilet kırk beş lira' states the price directly. Turkish drops the linking verb here.

english: Congratulations on your new job!
tip: 'olsun' is the let-it-be form of 'olmak': 'kutlu olsun' literally means may it be blessed, the way you congratulate.

english: We are tired after the long trip.
tip: 'sonra' (after) takes the '-tan' ending on the noun: 'yolculuk' becomes 'yolculuktan', so 'yolculuktan sonra' means after the trip.

english: We will go to the garden soon.
tip: Motion toward a place uses '-e': 'bahçe' becomes 'bahçeye', meaning to the garden.

english: You started at home the previous day.
tip: Location uses '-de': 'ev' plus '-de' gives 'evde', at home. It answers where something happens.

english: The students' homework is very difficult.
tip: To show whose, the owner takes '-in' and the thing takes '-i': 'öğrencilerin ödevleri' means the students' homework.

english: The writer finished the poem at school.
tip: 'bit-' alone means end by itself; add '-ir' to give it a doer: 'bitirdi' means he finished it, not just it ended.

english: We have been studying Turkish for two years.
tip: For a span of time up to now, add '-dir' to the amount: 'iki yıldır' means for two years now.

english: When I retire I will live in a village.
tip: '-ınca' means when or once: 'emekli ol' plus '-unca' gives 'olunca', once I retire. It sets the timing of the next clause.

english: I forgot the key, I can't open the door.
tip: '-muş' can mark a realization: 'unutmuşum' means it turns out I forgot, something you notice rather than state flatly.

english: This project will be very successful.
tip: For will be, Turkish uses 'olacak' ('olmak' plus future '-acak'): 'proje başarılı olacak' means the project will be successful.

english: Guests will come tonight, we must prepare.
tip: Obligation uses '-malı': 'yap' plus '-malı' plus '-yız' gives 'yapmalıyız', meaning we must prepare.
